articles.title: Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real
articles.summary:
There are plenty of reasons why Grand Theft Auto VI is so popular: the 13 years of anticipation, the relatable lead characters and romantic storyline, the sheer level of depth. But another major factor is the sense of place. The GTA series is unmatched when it comes to re-creating the feeling of a bustling, real-world city, and GTA VI’s fictional rendition of Florida is the studio’s most lifelike setting yet. It has functioning buses and trains, plentiful buildings you can go into and explore, residents you can chat with, and huge areas where you can interact with wildlife far away from the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City. For Emma Fraser, an assistant professor at UC Berkeley who studies urban ruins and virtual cities, the sense of realism has created a unique sensation while playing.
Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real
Virtual city expert Emma Fraser explains what makes Rockstar’s latest open world work.
“There’s something about this particular game that is really discombobulating and distracting in a sense,” she says. “Because you have these moments where you think, ‘I’m in a place, I’m experiencing a location.’ You comprehend intellectually that it’s not real or that it’s at best a representation, but you still have this feeling in your brain and you’ll still dream about being in that place.”

articles.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
articles.summary:
Password management and identity security company 1Password revealed on Wednesday that a hacker stole customer information and proprietary source code. 1Password says customer vaults are not affected.
The company launched an investigation on November 19 after discovering that an employee’s corporate GitHub account may have been compromised.
The attacker used the account to deploy malicious code to backend services and exfiltrate customer records. The compromised customer records include names, email addresses, account identifiers, public cryptographic keys, authentication parameters, account activity times, and non-secret metadata.
In addition, the threat actor obtained source code from private repositories and accessed the company’s CI/CD system, potentially exposing infrastructure credentials.
According to 1Password, the hacker also obtained tokens from emails sent to users for account invitations, provisioning, and recovery.
A “small number” of individuals who were undergoing provisioning or recovery during the intrusion have been notified. However, the company noted that the exposed tokens cannot be exploited on their own and there is no evidence that the attacker hijacked user accounts.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Drupal Installer Patch Left a Gap Attackers Are Already Exploiting
articles.summary:
Drupal says last week’s patch for an exploited installer vulnerability did not protect every website, and attackers are now leveraging the gap to hack vulnerable sites.
The new issue, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 with a CMSS score of 21/25, was disclosed on November 25, exactly a week after Drupal announced the original patch in advisory SA-CORE-2026-017. Drupal describes the new flaw as an access bypass issue that can lead to site takeover.
The update released on November 18 patched CVE-2026-132165, an installer flaw credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner. The affected installer ships with Drupal core and enables users to set up a new site.
Drupal was informed of in-the-wild exploitation soon after, and CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog on November 24.
The advisory for CVE-2026-136716 explains where the earlier fix fell short.
“SA-CORE-2026-017 recently fixed several vulnerabilities within the Drupal core installer. However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites,” Drupal said in its advisory.
It added, “It is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state, and sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state.”
Drupal warned that CVE-2026-136716 is being exploited in the wild and “any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.”

articles.title: GTA VI developers vote against unionization
articles.summary:
Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) said that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition.
GTA VI developers vote against unionization
Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.
Voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of GTA VI. If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implementation and layoffs. Without it, Rockstar won’t have an obligation to meet union representatives, though workers and union members can still lobby for change informally.
“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” IWGB said in a statement sent to The Verge. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”

Le message a depuis été supprimé par la modération, mais les vidéos ont eu le temps de circuler. Malgré le nom affiché à l’écran (« PS5 Pro 60 FPS Patch »), l’auteur reconnaît que son outil se contente de relever le plafond, sans atteindre un 60 FPS stable.

articles.title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Series SSD with Over 18 Million Random Read IOPS
articles.summary:
Kioxia is introducing the GP2 Series SSD, and the standout number is more than 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size. I think we actually saw a precursor to this drive a few weeks ago. 18M IOPS is nearly double the performance of the GP1 Series Kioxia showed in August at FMS. The new drive is designed for PCIe 6.0 and NVMe 2.3, and Kioxia says it is also expecting sequential read throughput of up to 28GB/s, enough to saturate a PCIe 6.0 x4 link.
Kioxia GP2 Series Launched
The GP series is designed for a specific role in AI systems. Instead of adding more expensive HBM or DRAM to a GPU system, operators can use these NAND-based drives to create a flash-based memory tier the GPU can access directly. This lets the system handle larger datasets at a lower cost. Whenever you try to replace DRAM with NAND, endurance becomes a question. At 50DWPD, the GP2 is a step above many of the common capacity-focused drives.

|---|---|
| Interface | PCIe 6.0 / NVMe 2.3 |

articles.title: From selling drones to intelligence: Where will the next wave of value come from?
articles.summary:
From selling drones to intelligence: Where will the next wave of value come from?
As the drone industry evolves, the focus is shifting from aircraft specifications to the value delivered to customers. The next phase of growth will be shaped by AI, software, integrated technologies and service-led business models.
When we look at the value of a drone, it is easy to focus on the aircraft itself. How long can it fly? How much weight can it carry? How far can it travel? These are important questions, and they will continue to matter. But there is another question that deserves equal attention: what does the customer actually get from that flight?
A drone may spend several hours monitoring an area and return with a large volume of footage. Yet, if the operator has to spend several more hours reviewing that footage to identify something important, much of the benefit is lost. The real value lies not simply in collecting information, but in making sense of it and using it at the right time.
I believe this is where the next phase of the drone industry will take shape.
The value does not end when the drone lands
As drones become more widely used across defence, infrastructure, mapping, and homeland security, customer expectations are changing. Buying a drone is increasingly becoming the beginning of a larger operational requirement.
Consider a team monitoring a long stretch of border or inspecting a large infrastructure project. The drone can capture images, video and location data, b…

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors exploited several Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities as zero-days in a data theft campaign, according to Accenture’s Apex Labs. CISA on Wednesday added five MiCollab flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
In one attack observed by Accenture, hackers gained privileged access to a MiCollab server and quickly reached the targeted organization’s identity infrastructure, ultimately stealing sensitive business information.
The MiCollab business collaboration platform enables employees to communicate through calls, messages, and virtual meetings. Accenture noted that the product’s frequent internet exposure and integration with Active Directory make it particularly attractive to hackers.
Mitel on November 16 announced patches for five vulnerabilities affecting the product’s audio, web and video conferencing component, including arbitrary file upload, XML injection, unauthorized access, command injection, and authentication bypass. They can all be exploited by unauthenticated attackers, and two critical bugs allow arbitrary command execution.

articles.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook

A new version of the SYS01 infostealer malware delivered through Meta ads is enrolling browsers into enterprise-style management to force the installation of an extension that steals sensitive data, including Gmail and Outlook emails.
The ads lure Windows users into downloading free animated wallpapers that work as advertised but also deploy malware in the background during installation.
The campaign targets Facebook and Meta business accounts and gives the operator access to recent Gmail and Outlook messages in Chrome, and the ability to permanently delete emails.
Bitdefender Labs tracks the campaign as SYS010 and says the malware is likely a new version of the SYS01 infostealer, observed since at least 2022 in malvertising activity on Facebook.
The name reflects the researchers' assessment that this variant represents a major improvement over its predecessor, leading them to tag it as version 2, represented in binary as 010.
Researchers identified a malicious SYS010 ad on October 16 and found that the campaign was still ongoing, with hundreds of ads created.
Company telemetry shows that requests to the threat actor’s servers came from several countries in Asia, Europe, North America, Africa, and South America.
Meta Ad Library' transparency page shows that one advertisement alone reached 6,275 users in the European Union, targeting anyone above 18.

En clair, ARTEX devait aider les experts en cybersécurité à débusquer les failles avant les pirates. Publié en libre accès sur Github, le logiciel a été promptement détourné par des cybercriminels. Branché sur des modèles d’IA chinois, comme DeepSeek, ARTEX peut orchestrer des attaques en toute autonomie, sans la moindre intervention initiale.
Des pirates s’en sont donc servis pour dérober les données personnelles d’environ 67 000 personnes en s’attaquant à des banques sud-coréennes. Les attaques se sont multipliées jusqu’à ce que le FBI publie une alerte officielle, assurant qu’« ARTEX réduit considérablement le temps nécessaire pour enchaîner les techniques d’attaque, certaines intrusions passant du ciblage initial à un accès privilégié en moins de trois heures ».
Dos au mur, le développeur Autumn-27 n’a pas tardé à retirer ARTEX de GitHub, mais des copies circulent toujours. En dépit de son retrait, ARTEX s’est retrouvé impliqué dans la cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne, qui a obligé l’institution à couper une partie de ses systèmes pendant dix jours. En interne, la Commission soupçonne des pirates soutenus par la Chine.

articles.title: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension

The Remus infostealer is stealing Gmail messages through a stealthy malicious Chrome extension, a capability the malware operators marketed as a zero-day exploit in Google's email service.
On November 8, the Remus infostealer developer started advertising the alleged Gmail zero-day flaw that allowed the malware to collect emails even if victims changed their passwords and revoked all sessions.
Threat intelligence company Hudson Rock investigated the claims but came to inconclusive results. The researchers noted that evidence from the malware customers matched the seller's pitch, although there was no technical proof that a zero-day vulnerability was being exploited.
GenDigital and Invoke RE researchers published their independent findings yesterday, explaining that the advertised “zero-day” was just a malicious Chrome extension installed on the victims' browsers.
The extension is designed to steal unread emails from signed-in Gmail accounts. It can also survive password changes and session revocations because it remains installed in the victim's Chrome browser.
Its access to Gmail stops when the active session ends, and resumes again when the victim signs back in.
GenDigital discovered the extension after reverse-engineering the Remus infostealer. The researchers found no trace of an email-stealing module, suggesting that the functionality is implemented via an add-on.

In one attack, a phishing email sent through HireVue invited recipients to attend a Google Cloud webinar about deploying AI applications into production.

It affects the Session Smart Conductor’s AutomatedProvisioner service and could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges via a specially crafted Salt minion ID.
A centralized management and policy solution, Session Smart Conductor is used for the orchestration and management of Session Smart Routers across networks. The Salt minion ID is a router’s unique ID when registering with the Salt master (Session Smart Conductor).
CVE-2026-103406 was patched on October 28 along with 17 other flaws in Session Smart Router and Session Smart Conductor. On Tuesday, Juniper updated its advisory to flag the security defect as exploited.
“At least one instance of malicious exploitation of CVE-2026-103406 has been reported to the Juniper SIRT. Customers are encouraged to upgrade to a fixed release as soon as possible and in the meantime take steps to mitigate this vulnerability,” reads Juniper’s update.
On Wednesday, CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, urging federal agencies to patch it within three days, as mandated by BOD 26-04.

“FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data,” the governing body said in its statement. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”
The breach comes at a time when FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, is under scrutiny after his foiled, secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino is also trying to extend his 11-year presidency of FIFA to 2031. He is the favorite when the election is held on March 18, with Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France the other candidates.

articles.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
articles.summary:
A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges.
Found by ANSSI's Jérémy Jean (who submitted a fix in August), the flaw has been dubbed NFS2ROOT by cybersecurity firm OpenSec, which shared a full remote-root exploit and a patch with the NFSD maintainers in late September.
The vulnerability has existed since Linux kernel version 3.16 (released in March 2014), and it stems from a heap buffer overflow weakness in the Linux NFS server (nfsd).
NFS2ROOT affects systems with a Linux kernel older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, or 7.4-rc1 if nfsd (v4.1 or 4.2) is loaded and running and TCP port 2049 is reachable over the Internet.
Successful exploitation lets remote threat actors without privileges corrupt kernel memory and gain root access to vulnerable Linux servers exposed online through low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction.
In NFS2ROOT attacks, the threat actors can exploit this flaw by sending maliciously crafted requests that cause the NFS server to write data beyond an allocated memory buffer. This lets them read kernel memory, bypass KASLR (which protects kernel memory addresses), and place a callback that can execute a command in a released memory area.
When the attacker closes the NFS connection, the kernel executes the embedded command with root privileges, allowing the attacker to gain root control of the unpatched Linux server.

Esta subida en el coste de la memoria viene como consecuencia de la gran demanda de chips por parte de las empresas tecnológicas para alimentar antes que nadie sus centros de datos, lo que terminan por agotar todo el suministro de varios años consecutivos. Y las empresas de memoria, como no podía ser de otra manera, venden su producto al que mejor pague.

The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act, but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide.
Android app developers will soon have to share their address publicly
The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.
Developers have until February 1st 2027 to declare whether or not they’re a “trader” under UK and European law. Broadly speaking, Google says the definition applies if you earn revenue from your apps, especially if that revenue is regular or at high volume. Developers are exempt if their apps are only a hobby or non-commercial, or if they simply don’t publish them in the UK or Europe.
If they self-declare as a trader, developers’ contact details will be shared publicly starting March 1st, including a phone number and address. articles.title: Friedrich Nietzsche, filósofo: “A menudo contradecimos una opinión cuando en realidad solo nos resulta desagradable el tono con que fue expresada”
articles.summary:
Friedrich Nietzsche constató que uno de los problemas de las conversaciones es que a veces odiamos la opinión de alguien por el tono que usa. “A menudo contradecimos una opinión cuando en realidad solo nos resulta desagradable el tono con que fue expresada”, escribió en el aforismo 303 de Humano, demasiado humano. Así aparece en el libro.
Se publicó en 1878. Por entonces, el filósofo alemán se alejaba del pensamiento de Schopenhauer. También estaba en peores términos con Richard Wagner (de quien había sido amigo). En la obra analizó las motivaciones de los seres humanos y puso en cuestión la idea de que nuestras opiniones vienen de un proceso racional por encima de los afectos.
Es entonces cuando hace esta observación sobre el tono. Podemos contradecir una opinión aunque realmente lo que desagrade sea el tono de la persona que afirma algo. Es una de las reacciones habituales, aunque Nietzsche no afirma que sean la mayoría de los casos de desacuerdo.
Asoció las creencias con el temperamento. En el aforismo 608 escribió que buscamos inconscientemente principios y doctrinas que se adapten a nuestro modo de ser. Incluso podemos decir después que son estas ideas las que han dado forma a nuestro carácter (aunque Nietzsche dijo lo contrario).
En el 571 escribió también que cuando nos hacen una pregunta, de pronto la primera opinión que tenemos es la que suele ser habitual en nuestro grupo/posición/origen. Para Nietzsche esto no necesariamente era una opinión propia.

articles.title: Qué electrodomésticos consumen más energía y cómo reducir la factura de luz en casa
articles.summary:
La nevera, la secadora, el horno eléctrico, la lavadora y la plancha figuran entre los electrodomésticos que más energía consumen en casa, aunque el impacto final sobre la factura de luz depende de la potencia, el tiempo de uso y los hábitos de cada familia. Identificar qué equipos permanecen conectados durante más horas permite detectar dónde conviene actuar primero.
El consumo eléctrico no depende solo de los aparatos más grandes. Una secadora puede gastar mucha energía en poco tiempo, mientras una nevera mantiene un gasto continuo durante todo el día. Conocer esa diferencia ayuda a ajustar rutinas, aprovechar programas eficientes y evitar gastos innecesarios sin dejar de utilizar los equipos necesarios en el hogar.
La potencia y el tiempo explican el consumo
La fórmula básica para entender el gasto energético es sencilla: consumo igual a potencia multiplicada por tiempo de uso. Un aparato de alta potencia puede elevar la factura aunque se utilice pocos minutos, mientras otro menos exigente puede acumular consumo si permanece encendido de forma constante.
También importa la frecuencia. La lavadora, por ejemplo, puede tener un impacto moderado si se utiliza pocas veces por semana y con carga completa. El gasto crece cuando se realizan ciclos pequeños, se selecciona agua caliente o se repiten lavados innecesarios. El hábito tiene tanto peso como el electrodoméstico.

articles.title: How Much Does Coram AI Cost? Pricing, Licences and What's Included

If you’ve been looking at AI security camera platforms, you’ve probably noticed Coram AI doesn’t put a price on its website. So how much does it actually cost?
Here’s the short answer. Coram AI doesn’t publish a price list. Its pricing is quote-based and depends on three things: how many locations you have, the type of cameras you’re using, and how many days of video you want to keep. Every order includes an on-site appliance called Coram Point, which you buy upfront and own, plus a per-camera software licence on a one, three, five or 10-year term.
That might sound vague, but the way the price is built is actually quite clear. Here’s what goes into a Coram quote, what you get for it and what costs extra.
Why Coram doesn’t publish a price
Coram is an AI physical security platform used by schools, healthcare groups, warehouses and multi-site businesses. Because no two sites are the same, Coram prices each deployment based on its real requirements rather than a one-size-fits-all plan.
The three inputs are simple. The number of locations decides how many Coram Point appliances you need. The type of camera affects how many video feeds each appliance has to handle. And the days of storage you need decides how much recording capacity goes on site. Coram says that once its sales team has those three details, it can come back with a price quickly.
Quotes are in US dollars, so Australian buyers should factor in the exchange rate on the day.

Hex, the package manager for Elixir and Erlang, fell victim to a cyberattack involving unauthorized access to its web servers.
The incident occurred on November 23, when the attackers exploited a vulnerability in hex.pm to execute commands. The attack was immediately blocked, and the underlying security defect was addressed within 20 minutes.
Between 18:16 and 18:29 UTC, the attacker sent 69 malicious requests, affecting six web servers. At 18:30, Hex replaced all hex.pm servers with patched versions rejecting the payload, and its firewall rule fully blocked the attacker’s traffic at 18:33.
“We found no evidence of unauthorized package modifications, database changes, or that the attacker maintained access to our systems,” the package manager explains.
According to Hex, potential access to database contents, such as email addresses, password hashes, API key hashes, sessions, second factor authentication secrets, and audit logs, cannot be ruled out.
While all the observed reads of private packages came from Hex servers, any read from a compromised server would appear legitimate, it says. Additionally, database and private documentation reads are not logged, hindering visibility into potential data exposure.
“The attacker’s commands could read the credentials our servers use, so we replaced them: the storage, CDN, email and database credentials, and the keys that sign sessions and access tokens. This logged everyone out of hex.pm and Hex clients,” Hex notes.

More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. articles.title: What Happens to Your Returned Gadget? The Hidden Journey of Electronics Returns
articles.summary:
You return a laptop that “just stopped working”. The shop scans the box, hands over a refund and you walk out feeling lighter. Two weeks later, where is that laptop?
Most of us never think about it. But what happens next decides whether the thing gets a second life or ends up in a skip bin. It also shapes the price you pay for new gear, how fair warranty decisions are, and how much e-waste Australia produces. Here’s the journey, step by step.
Why a returned electronic isn’t like a returned jumper
Behind every returned gadget is a process of paperwork, tracking and decisions that most shoppers never see
A jumper goes back on the rack. A laptop doesn’t. Someone has to confirm the serial number, check whether the fault is real, wipe your data, reset the firmware and decide if the battery is safe to ship. Skip any of those and the retailer either resells a dud or throws away a perfectly good machine.
That’s why businesses that sell tech at any scale often bring in dedicated electronics returns management services to handle the messy middle: RMA intake, inspection, functional testing and the call on what happens next. It’s a model that suits retailers, brands and integrators alike, because the work is repetitive, technical and easy to get wrong when it’s squeezed in between everything else a warehouse does.

Un pilote vulnérable, mais légitime, distribué par Windows Update
C’est après avoir mis à jour un système Intel NUC de 11e génération que Deskmodder a vu s’afficher une alerte de sécurité émise par Microsoft Defender. Celle-ci a mis en lumière un problème provenant du paquet Intel Performance Driver Extension dans sa version 1.0.0.38. Ce module lié au service Intel NUC Software Studio Service et qui a pour objectif de fournir une surveillance matérielle de bas niveau, comporte une importante faille de sécurité. Une brèche qui touche plus particulièrement le composant WinRing0 de ce pilote et dont la vulnérabilité est connue depuis 2020.
Cette faille, identifiée sous la référence CVE-2020-14979 permet une élévation locale des privilèges. Cela signifie concrètement que des attaquants disposant déjà d’un accès à la machine pourraient exploiter ce pilote légitime pour mener des attaques de type Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver et ainsi contourner les protections du noyau de Windows.
Windows Update réinstalle automatiquement le pilote après suppression

articles.title: After a decade in Nigeria, Bolt is looking beyond rides
articles.summary:
When Bolt, the Estonian mobility company, launched as Taxify in Lagos in November 2016, it entered a market where Uber, the American ride-hailing giant, had already established a lead after arriving two years earlier.
By July 2016, Uber had completed more than one million trips across Lagos and Abuja. Taxify was not only competing with an established rival; it also had to win commuters over from yellow taxis and public transportation by offering another way to get around.
A decade later, Nigeria’s ride-hailing market looks very different. Yellow taxis have lost most of their prominence, while the market has attracted other international players like inDrive, and local operators such as LagRide and Rida. In September, Uber announced it was winding down its Nigerian operations, marking the exit of the company that had once led the market.
Meanwhile, Bolt has expanded its footprint to 31 cities and says it has reached more than 14 million riders in Nigeria since it entered the market. The company also says it has invested more than ₦140 billion ($102.4 million) in the country. Beyond ride-hailing, it has expanded into other ride categories, vehicle financing, food delivery and electric mobility.
Early beginnings and price wars
Weyinmi Aghadiuno, Bolt’s Head of Regulatory and Policy, Africa, said Bolt entered into Nigeria at a time when getting around the country’s cities was often unpredictable.

The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
Avi Davidson is the first at-home user of an experimental prosthetic hand that lets him feel his wife’s hand in his own.
Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand.
Davidson, who is taking part in a clinical trial run by the University of Utah, is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted in his arm. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently.
The hand is part of the bionic LUKE arm, named after Luke Skywalker of Star Wars, who was fitted with a lifelike prosthetic arm after his own was light-sabered off. The arm was developed in the 2000s, initially trialed in 2014, and approved by the FDA that same year. The trial that Davidson is enrolled in isn’t so focused on the arm itself but on a new way to connect it to a person’s nervous system. The connection allows users to control movements and receive feedback about how much pressure they’re applying.
Researchers hope that Davidson’s experiences will help them answer some long-standing questions about the technology, including how useful it really is in day-to-day life. They want to know when the device is helpful and where it might fail. They…

articles.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
articles.summary:
Mock Service Worker, the API mocking library maintained by Artem Zakharchenko, has released version 3.0, nearly three years after the Fetch-based v2.0 rewrite. The release ships as ESM-only, completes the library's GraphQL story with subscription support, and introduces a socket-based interception algorithm in Node.js that Zakharchenko describes as going as deep into the runtime as JavaScript will allow without recompiling Node.
The headline breaking change is that MSW is now distributed natively as ECMAScript Modules only, with support for Node.js v18 and v20 dropped in favour of v22, v24, and v26. TypeScript 5.9 is now the minimum supported version. Several transitive dependencies have been removed, including graphql (now a proper optional peer), path-to-regexp, picocolors, and statuses. The result is a library tarball that drops from 416KB to 234KB, with type definitions shrinking by half, from 190KB to 90KB.
Alongside ESM, v3.0 introduces granular entrypoints that replace the single msw import with designated paths for each protocol:
import { http } from 'msw/http'
import { graphql } from 'msw/graphql'
import { sse } from 'msw/sse'
import { ws } from 'msw/ws'
GraphQL subscription support, a long-standing community request on the project's tracker, lands in this release. Building on the WebSocket interception shipped previously, subscription handlers can now be defined against a graphql.link() and publish events on demand, closing the gap between MSW's HTTP, WebSocket, and…

The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) has disclosed a data breach impacting data that residents uploaded to the myColorado application.
Colorado’s official mobile application, myColorado is used for digital identification, state services, and document storage. It has approximately 2.1 million users.
OIT took the application offline last week, after identifying unauthorized access to platform data, and immediately initiated incident response and an investigation into the incident.
One week after the outage began, OIT said it discovered the incident after the attackers triggered the automated threat detection systems deployed within its Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment.
The investigation has determined that the attackers accessed documents stored within the ‘myCards and Documents’ section of the application, which includes user-uploaded data, such as PDF files and photos of government IDs, vehicle registrations, and insurance cards.
According to Colorado, approximately 100,000 individuals might have been affected, but no payment information was accessed.
“Staff are working around the clock to match the inappropriately accessed documents to individual users. As that matching continues, OIT will further refine estimates on the number of people whose data was involved,” Colorado said.

Pour se faire pardonner, la start-up de Sam Altman offre une réinitialisation de quota supplémentaire aux abonnés Go, Plus, Pro et Business.
Au lancement de GPT-6.2 Astra et Sol, le 17 novembre, OpenAI promettait que Sol vous laisserait accomplir davantage de tâches avec votre abonnement payant. articles.title: Your Google Meet calls are about to get a little clearer

If you spend a lot of time on Google Meet, you might soon notice that everyone’s video looks a little better. Why? Google is finally upgrading users to higher-res video.
According to an update on the Google Workspace blog, the search giant revealed that it would expand 1080p video sending to Meet on the web for all users. Previously, Full HD video was limited to select paying users, and 1080p receiving was already available to all.
Now, everyone with a computer sporting a 1080p camera and sufficient compute and bandwidth will automatically have 1080p video sending. However, Workspace administrators can set different video quality defaults, so some people might not see the higher resolution depending on their workspace settings. Video settings can be adjusted by heading to Settings > Video.
Google also noted that Meet automatically scales resolution according to the size of the video tiles. In other words, when more people are in the meeting and the video tiles are smaller, it will reduce the resolution accordingly so it doesn’t burn unnecessary CPU or bandwidth.
It’s also worth noting that 1080p video is limited to those using Chromium-based browsers like Google’s own Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, or others. Non-Chromium browsers like Safari or Firefox won’t have 1080p video.
The search giant didn’t clarify in the blog post if there would be changes to Meet on mobile devices. Currently, smartphones can receive 1080p video, but can only transmit 720p video. Hopefully…

Indian SMBs with in-house AI talent grew their teams 5.2 percentage points faster in H1 2026, more than double the global gap. Yet only 6% have everyday AI skills across their workforce, a new Zoho and LinkedIn report finds.

It combines LinkedIn network data from more than 1.4 billion members, including over 193 million in India, with usage data from more than 78,000 organisations on Zoho Workplace, Zoho People and Bigin by Zoho CRM. It defines an SMB as an India-headquartered business with 11 to 200 employees. The work spanned seven previews and a release candidate, and the documentation describes product quality as the release's focus. Overall, this release consolidates more than it expands.
.NET MAUI (Multi-platform App UI) is Microsoft's cross-platform UI framework for Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows apps built from one C# and XAML codebase. .NET 11 is a Standard Term Support release with two years of support. Microsoft notes that MAUI follows its own support policy, separate from the runtime's STS and LTS lifecycle.
The runtime switch is the most significant change. According to Microsoft, CoreCLR puts mobile and desktop apps on the same runtime as the other .NET workloads. Release builds use composite partial ReadyToRun by default. On Apple platforms, which disallow JIT compilation, code that isn't precompiled runs in the CoreCLR interpreter. Native AOT is an opt-in publishing option, and its Android support is still experimental. Microsoft recommends developers to test app libraries before choosing their deployment model.

articles.title: 1Password confirms data breach after hacker compromises employee's GitHub account
articles.summary:
What we know so far: 1Password has confirmed that a hacker stole customer names and email addresses from its backend systems. The attacker compromised a single employee's GitHub account and was able to push malicious code into those services and pull customer records. The stolen data does not include passwords or anything stored in customer vaults, but it still leaves users open to convincing phishing attempts, and 1Password has not said how many people are affected.
1Password began its investigation earlier this month. By then, the intruder had used the hijacked account to browse the company's source code and insert malicious instructions designed to collect customer data.
The change was a subtle one. Code written to look like part of the normal system doesn't need to break anything, and one compromised developer login was enough to put it into production. Attacks on source repositories and build pipelines have become a common route into software companies, and this one fits that pattern.
Beyond names and email addresses, the haul included public keys and the account and user identifiers that 1Password uses internally. Public keys are designed to be shared, so exposing them doesn't hand over access to anything. The identifiers could still help someone build a more believable lure or match records to a particular customer.

articles.title: Científicos recuperan bajo la Antártida un archivo geológico de entre 17 y 19 millones de años tras dos intentos fallidos y atravesar 523 metros de hielo
articles.summary:
Bajo el hielo de la Antártida occidental se encuentran sedimentos que son los que nos indican cómo era esta zona antes de que quedara bajo el hielo. Para ello han tenido que trabajar en un campamento que queda a unos 700 km de las bases antárticas más cercanas. En Crary Ice Rise han conseguido sacar un núcleo de 228 m de longitud de barro y roca. Hasta ahora habían fallado en dos intentos.
Tras perforar 523 metros de hielo, han conseguido recuperar materiales de millones de años de antigüedad. Han analizado los microfósiles de los sedimentos y los más antiguos se remontan hasta hace entre 17 y 19 millones de años. Se trata de los últimos 20 m de la perforación sedimentaria. La mayor parte del núcleo está entre los 7 y los 10 millones de años.
Esto forma parte del proyecto internacional SWAIS2C, que trata de conocer la sensibilidad de la capa de hielo de la Antártida occidental ante un calentamiento de 2 grados Celsius. Los responsables del proyecto pretenden conocer qué pasó en esta zona en épocas cálidas del pasado para poder mejorar las predicciones de su respuesta al calentamiento global.
Primero el hielo, después los sedimentos
Para ello, primero han tenido que crear un agujero en el hielo mediante una técnica de perforación con agua caliente. Una vez hecho el agujero, han podido colocar las tuberías para extraer los materiales del subsuelo. En el comunicado de la expedición destacan que han trabajado en rotación durante las 24 horas del día.

L’agence n’a précisé ni la manière dont les pirates sont entrés, ni s’ils ont pu accéder à des données. Elle ne sait pas non plus qui est derrière l’opération.

Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.

Después de la conjetura de Riemann, de VP ≠ VNP o la multiplicación de matrices, ahora hay investigadores que (a lomos de la IA) quieren unificar la física cuántica y la teoría de la relatividad (al menos en aspectos sustanciales). Pero vayamos por partes.
Una teoría cuántica de la gravedad. La relatividad general describe la gravedad como la forma del espacio-tiempo; la mecánica cuántica describe el resto de fuerzas y la materia. Se suele decir que la primera se encarga de lo muy grande y la segunda de lo muy pequeño: unificarlas conllevaría estar muy cerca de una teoría del todo. Una herramienta que permita explicar toda la realidad.
Pero, tranquilos, aún no hemos llegado a eso. Durante décadas se ha tratado de juntar ambas teorías de una forma u otra. Por ejemplo, una receta habitual consiste en fijar un espacio-tiempo de fondo y cuantizar las pequeñas ondulaciones que lo recorren (cuyos cuantos serían los gravitones).
La idea es buena y, de hecho, funciona a baja energía. Pero en cuanto se afina el cálculo, aparecen infinitos que no hay manera de esconder debajo de controlar.
A este callejón llegamos en 1985 y en él seguimos.

articles.title: SaaS Sprawl Is Becoming a Project Delivery Problem: How Distributed Teams Keep Work Connected
articles.summary:
For many organisations, adopting another cloud application no longer feels like a technology decision. A new communication platform solves one problem, a specialist tool improves another workflow, a shared drive handles documents, spreadsheets fill reporting gaps and a separate system tracks resources or budgets.
Each addition can be perfectly rational. The difficulty appears later, when the work itself has to move across all of them. A project manager may receive an important decision in chat, update a deadline in a task tool, confirm resource availability in a spreadsheet and then recreate the same situation in a management report. Nothing is necessarily missing, yet the overall picture becomes harder to trust.
This is the operational side of SaaS sprawl. The issue is not simply that a business pays for too many subscriptions. It is that project context becomes distributed across tools at the same time as the teams doing the work become distributed across locations. Hybrid and international teams are particularly exposed because informal coordination is already more difficult. When colleagues cannot resolve an ambiguity by turning to the person sitting next to them, every missing decision, outdated status or unclear handoff has more opportunity to become a delay.
More tools can create less visibility

articles.title: How PCB Design Affects Battery Life in Smart Home Devices
articles.summary:
Smart home devices are becoming part of everyday life. From wireless door sensors and smart locks to temperature monitors and security systems, many connected devices promise months or even years of operation without needing a battery replacement.
Yet battery life can vary significantly between products that appear to perform similar functions.
While battery capacity is an obvious factor, the electronics inside a device play an equally important role. Power management, wireless communication, component selection, and printed circuit board (PCB) design all influence how efficiently a smart device uses energy.
Understanding these factors helps explain why some devices last longer than others.
1. The Hidden Power Consumption Inside Smart Devices
A smart home sensor may appear inactive for most of the day, but its internal electronics are rarely completely switched off.
Even when the device is not actively collecting or transmitting data, certain components may continue drawing small amounts of current.
Typical power consumers include:
- Microcontrollers responsible for processing sensor information
- Wireless communication chips
- Voltage regulators and power management circuits
- Sensors and monitoring components
- Status indicators and supporting circuitry
The total energy consumption depends on both how much current these components draw and how long they remain active.

articles.title: 9:16 o 16:9: qué formato elegir para publicar videos o reels
articles.summary:
Una duda común entre quienes crean contenido para YouTube, Instagram, Facebook o TikTok es si conviene grabar y publicar un video en 9:16 o en 16:9. La elección no depende solo de una preferencia estética: define cómo se verá la pieza en pantalla, qué espacio ocupará en el feed y qué tipo de experiencia tendrá el público.
Los dos formatos responden a usos distintos. El 9:16 es vertical y está pensado para celulares; el 16:9 es horizontal y conserva el esquema tradicional de pantallas de televisión, computadoras y videos de YouTube. Antes de encender la cámara, hay que definir la plataforma principal, la duración y el material que se quiere mostrar.
Qué diferencias existen entre 9:16 y 16:9
El formato 9:16 tiene una relación de aspecto vertical: por cada nueve unidades de ancho, la imagen cuenta con 16 de alto. Una resolución habitual es 1.080 por 1.920 píxeles. Ocupa casi toda la pantalla de un celular cuando se sostiene en posición vertical, así que reduce las distracciones y favorece una visualización rápida.
El 16:9 invierte esa proporción. Es un formato horizontal, con resoluciones frecuentes de 1.920 por 1.080 píxeles o 3.840 por 2.160 píxeles en 4K. Ofrece un campo visual más amplio y permite mostrar paisajes, entrevistas con varias personas, demostraciones de productos, deportes o escenas en las que el ambiente aporta información.

A ideia da empresa é montar uma constelação de computadores na órbita da Terra, formando uma espécie de data center orbital para rodar, sobretudo, os trabalhos de IA ao redor do planeta.
Os modelos enviados ao espaço seriam alimentados por energia solar, o que resolveria o alto consumo exigido desses servidores em Terra. Outra vantagem seria a baixa temperatura, que serviria para arrefecer as máquinas durante o processamento de dados. Da mesma forma, ao fragmentar esse trabalho em milhões de satélites, a geração de calor seria menor do que em Terra.
Ainda assim, especialistas da área apontam diversos empecilhos para que os planos deem certo. Segundo a Associated Press, o astrofísico e autor Adam Becker classifica o projeto como uma “fantasia”, destacando problemas simples de física como impeditivos. A existência de vácuo, por exemplo, causaria retenção do calor gerado, independente da temperatura ao redor. Além disso, os riscos de colisão e poluição atmosféricas também são lembrados entre as críticas.

- Share:
Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. But a very different category of matter can draw on its own energy to change shape and respond to outside forces in surprising ways. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Now, physicists from the universities of Amsterdam, New South Wales, and Cambridge have uncovered remarkable new behaviors that could change how future machines and robots are designed.
Everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: How to Kill the Code Review
articles.summary:
Closing the Engineering the Developer Experience track at QCon San Francisco 2026, Ankit Jain, co-founder and CEO of Aviator, argued that line-by-line code review is already quietly dead on most teams, and that the sharper question is "how long until we stop reading the code?" He also flagged his conflict of interest up front, noting that he runs a company that sells a solution and asking the audience to "be suspicious of me."
The talk revisited an essay he wrote for Latent Space in March 2026 proposing a five-layer trust model to replace reviews. Eight months on, Jain said the mechanics held up but the essay missed human judgment entirely. He began with the data that unseated his original framing. A 2013 Microsoft study found 44% of reviewers cited defect-finding as their motivation, yet only 14% of their comments were actually about defects, and a 2018 Google study of more than nine million reviews reached almost the same split. Code review was never really about bugs, he argued, it was about knowledge sharing, echoing Addy Osmani: "We made writing cheap, and understanding stayed exactly as expensive as it has always been."
A September Faros study of more than 4,000 teams found that over 75% of PRs now merge without any human review, average PR size has grown, and redo work is up 67% year over year. Earlier research showed review quality drops sharply past 400 lines, yet the median PR today is 640 lines. "We are reviewing the code, but we are rubber stamping it," Jain said,…

You have a single code base, unified development process, and one small team responsible for that. The point when you choose to hire React Native developers or migrate to Flutter marks the beginning of another challenge – to find a partner who will not sacrifice quality on one platform in favor of the other.
React Native is the right choice for companies that have experience writing in JavaScript and React and also want to access a vast array of library support. La vidéo est cruelle pour Rockstar : GTA Online ne sortirait pas avant fin 2027. La sphère pirate pourrait créer sa propre version du jeu des mois en avance et perturber le lancement du jeu.

articles.title: Telus met with Quebecor over sale, but concerns remain
articles.summary:
Telus has finally provided an update following the highly publicized meeting with Quebecor.
Speaking at the Desjardins Toronto conference on Tuesday, Telus CFO Gopi Chande confirmed that executives from the two companies met to discuss Quebecor’s proposed acquisition.
For context, Quebecor proposed two deals to Telus’ board (the most recent on Nov. 9), with CEO Pierre Karl Peladeau citing SpaceX and American competition as the motive for the proposal.
Chande described the meeting as “pleasant,” but stressed that the company has not reached a decision yet. Similarly, Quebecor said separately that it was encouraged by the willingness to continue discussions, but neither company has announced a deal.
Telus has four major concerns with the proposal: regulatory approval, voting control (governance structure), leverage (financial implications), and valuation (whether the offer adequately values Telus).
Planhub says that all four issues were discussed during the meeting.
Interestingly, it was also noted that Telus will continue moving forward with its own restructuring plan. This includes its $900 million annual improvement in free cash flow by the end of 2028, with approximately 80 per cent of that coming from its telecom operations. The restructuring plan also includes the sale of Telus Health, which is reportedly close to being sold, while Telus Agriculture is also under consideration for sale.

Source: Planhub

First look: A television's backlight usually starts as white light that a color filter then splits into red, green, and blue. Seoul Semiconductor wants to drop that step by placing individual red, green, and blue chips behind a standard LCD panel, spaced only tens of micrometers apart. The company says the approach, called WICOP Pixel, covers 100% of the DCI-P3 color gamut used in digital cinema, reaches peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits, and has now entered mass production.
The design comes from Seoul Viosys, a Seoul Semiconductor subsidiary. Its WICOP technology removes the conventional package, the housing that normally surrounds an LED die. The chip structure is robust enough to be handled like an ordinary electronic component. The technique was first applied to blue opto-semiconductors and has since been extended to green, red, and ultraviolet wavelengths.
WICOP Pixel combines several of those wavelengths in a single pixel unit. Each color is controlled independently and mixed precisely. The company says this reproduces tens of thousands of natural colors efficiently and vividly.
The performance claims are aimed squarely at OLED, which has long been the reference for premium picture quality. Seoul Semiconductor says peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits is more than three times what OLED delivers, and that the design lasts more than twice as long. Podemos pensar que cuando alguien baja al mismo bar todas las mañanas a desayunar pese a tener café y pan en casa lo hace por prisa o por tener pocas ganas de hacerse el desayuno. Pero algunos estudios psicológicos apuntan a que esos locales también parecen cubrir otras necesidades más allá de las gastronómicas.
Qué es un tercer lugar. Se llama así a cualquier espacio que no es ni la casa ni el trabajo y en el que la gente puede quedarse y encontrarse con otros hasta crear vínculos informales. Según un artículo de la revista Health & Place publicado en 2019, en esa categoría entran cafeterías, bares, bibliotecas, peluquerías o pequeños restaurantes.
Tres cafeterías bajo la lupa. La investigadora y especialista en diseño de interiores Lisa Waxman observó tres cafeterías durante 75 horas en total, hizo entrevistas y recogió encuestas de 94 clientes. En su estudio de 2006 en el Journal of Interior Design aparecieron una y otra vez temas como la pertenencia, la posibilidad de socializar, el apoyo, las redes de contactos, la productividad y la sensación de comunidad. Además, cuanto más tiempo llevaba alguien yendo al mismo café, más apegado se sentía a su comunidad.
Pero ese dato ayuda a entender por qué repetir sitio puede formar parte del atractivo, ya que quien desayuna siempre en el mismo bar acaba reconociendo al camarero y a otros habituales que, aunque quizá no lleguen a ser amigos, dejan de ser desconocidos.

articles.title: Engineering Reliable Telematics from Smartphone Sensors
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Smartphone GPS, motion sensors, and vehicle interfaces can each report valid measurements that produce incorrect results when combined without accounting for timing and coordinate frames.
- Preserve raw observations and their provenance before synchronizing, transforming, or normalizing them.
- Introduce a quality gate that determines whether telemetry is suitable for a particular decision instead of forcing every observation into a definitive result.
- Design for real-world conditions, including delayed GPS updates, phone movement, background interruptions, and intermittent connectivity.
- Monitor data quality alongside conventional application and infrastructure metrics because a functioning pipeline can still produce unreliable driving events.
Why this matters: the phone is not the vehicle
A smartphone can provide a surprising amount of information about a journey, including GPS estimates location and speed, accelerometers measure motion along the device's axes, gyroscopes capture rotation, and others. A connected vehicle may expose additional signals, such as speed, engine state, or diagnostic information.
Combining these sources creates opportunities for fleet monitoring, usage-based insurance, driving-behavior analysis, trip reconstruction, and connected mobility services.

articles.title: Ontario to crack down on e-bikes, some may need a licence
articles.summary:
Ontario is looking to strengthen regulations for electric bicycles (e-bikes) to stop motorcycle-style and motor-scooter-style electric vehicles from being used as e-bikes.
Starting May 1, 2027, only e-bikes that have a bicycle-style frame, fully operable pedals and a maximum speed of 32km/h will be allowed to be on Ontario roads without a driver’s licence, vehicle registration and insurance. If your e-bike doesn’t meet these requirements, you could face fines of up to $2,500 and vehicle impoundment.
Ontario is working with local law enforcement, municipalities, road safety partners, courier companies, manufacturers, retailers and the insurance industry to start raising awareness of Ontario’s new e-bike framework. Different municipalities may have more rules that may apply to e-bikes on local roads.
Some other rules include that e-bike users must be at least 16 years old, wear a helmet, and follow the same rules of the road as other cyclists. There are some more rules here.

Die Bundesregierung schlägt im Ringen um ein faires Urheberrecht im Zeitalter Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) ein neues europäisches Vergütungsmodell vor. Das geht aus einer Stellungnahme der Bundesregierung zur EU-Konsultation zum Urheberrecht hervor, die der Deutschen Presse-Agentur vorliegt. Anbieter generativer KI-Dienste sollen demnach künftig auch für die Erzeugung von Inhalten zahlen – etwa wenn ihre Systeme Texte, Musik oder Videos produzieren, die mit von Menschen geschaffenen Werken konkurrieren.
Deutschland und 14 weitere EU-Staaten hatten die EU-Kommission jüngst aufgefordert, möglichst rasch einen Gesetzesvorschlag zur Stärkung des Urheberrechts im Zeitalter Künstlicher Intelligenz vorzulegen.
Bisher wird vor allem darüber gestritten, unter welchen Bedingungen Firmen urheberrechtlich geschützte Inhalte zum Training von KI-Systemen nutzen dürfen. Die Bundesregierung schlägt nun einen neuen Vergütungsanspruch vor, der bei der Erzeugung von KI-Inhalten ansetzt. Aunque la escena suene bastante absurda, en realidad tiene todo el sentido porque forma parte de un experimento llevado a cabo por la South Florida Water Management District. Su objetivo es atraer a las serpientes invasoras que infestan los Everglades para que puedan ser capturadas y retiradas de la zona.
La tecnología entra en juego. Un ejemplar adulto puede medir hasta 6 metros de longitud, pero más que por su tamaño, el problema para capturarlas es que se camuflan demasiado bien y encontrarlas a simple vista es una tarea casi imposible. Aquí es donde entran en juego los conejitos robóticos que hacen que sea la serpiente la que salga de su escondite.
El esfuerzo de las autoridades da una idea de la dimensión del problema. Según la Comisión de Conservación de Pesca y Vida Silvestre de Florida, desde 2017 los equipos contratados por el estado y el organismo gestor del agua han retirado más de 19.000 pitones.

Aux États-Unis, une étude du MIT attribue environ 650 morts prématurées en 2023 à la pollution des centrales qui les alimentent. Les régions les plus touchées se trouvent souvent loin de la Virginie et du Texas, qui consomment pourtant l'essentiel de ce courant.
Des chercheurs du MIT, de l'université de Californie à Irvine et de Yale ont publié le 19 novembre dans Environmental Research Letters une estimation inédite. En 2023, la pollution de l'air due à l'électricité produite pour les centres de données américains aurait causé environ 650 décès prématurés : 513 attribués aux particules fines, 137 à l'ozone. C'est près de 5,3 % de la mortalité imputable à toute la production électrique du pays.
Quand on parle des nuisances des data centers, on pense d'abord aux riverains, comme ceux qui ont porté plainte contre le vacarme du centre de données d'Elon Musk. Noelle Selin, professeure au MIT qui a supervisé l'étude, invite à regarder plus loin : "Même si vous pensez ne pas être concerné parce qu'aucun data center ne se trouve près de chez vous, détrompez-vous."

articles.title: Cuál temperatura debe tener el aire acondicionado en invierno
articles.summary:
En países como España, la llegada del invierno no implica dejar de lado el aire acondicionado. Los electrodomésticos con bomba de calor permiten elevar la temperatura de las habitaciones durante los días fríos y pueden complementar otros sistemas de calefacción presentes en la vivienda.
La clave está en evitar ajustes extremos. La temperatura ideal del aire acondicionado en invierno se sitúa entre 20°C y 22°C, según Repsol, un rango que ayuda a compensar el frío exterior sin crear un ambiente excesivamente seco ni una diferencia térmica incómoda al salir o entrar del hogar.
Una diferencia moderada respecto de la temperatura de la calle evita que el ambiente sea sofocante. Al abrir una puerta o una ventana, el contraste entre el interior y el exterior puede aumentar la sensación de frío. Por eso, conviene sostener una regulación constante antes que encender y apagar el aparato de forma reiterada.
Cómo puede un aire acondicionado funcionar como calefacción
Muchos modelos cuentan con bomba de calor, una tecnología reversible que permite utilizar el mismo aparato en modo frío durante el verano y en modo calor en invierno. Esta función capta energía térmica del exterior y la traslada al interior para elevar la temperatura de las habitaciones.
Según Midea, este sistema puede generar hasta 4 kW de calor por cada 1 kW de energía eléctrica consumida, aunque el rendimiento concreto depende del modelo, el aislamiento de la vivienda y las condiciones meteorológicas.

articles.title: How often should you do maintenance on a Mac?
articles.summary:
Every Mac user knows that the operating system runs very well, and it can give you impressive performance for quite some time. But this is a machine and eventually there can be some problems which arise. Hence the reason why it makes sense to perform some maintenance. Now the question is, how often do you need to perform that maintenance? Here’s what you need to consider.
Does Mac OS maintain itself?
Yes, it does a lot of things in the background, on its own. The idea here is that it automates many tasks like clearing out expired temporary files, rebuilding internal databases or rotating system logs. All of that is made automatically in the background, which makes it incredibly rewarding and exciting as well, something to take into account.
Another thing that Mac OS does is it performs SSD Optimization. It trims the device in order to keep any file fragments close to one another. Doing so improves the overall speed of the device, and it leads to a way better and more consistent experience. Silicon Macs also have better RAM management and a system called unified memory. That’s excellent, and it truly helps enhance the experience in better ways than you might expect.
Things to do on a weekly basis
- A good idea is to wipe down the screen, keyboard and trackpad. It’s very easy for these to get dirty, so cleaning everything up is a very good idea.

Euro NCAP, l’organisme européen qui attribue les étoiles de sécurité aux voitures neuves, admet maintenant que ces alertes poussent les conducteurs à couper leurs aides, ce qui est contreproductif.
Dans un entretien accordé à Auto Express publié le 21 novembre, Matthew Avery, son directeur du développement stratégique, annonce que les voitures seront bientôt notées sur leur « facteur d’agacement ». L’organisme trouve aujourd’hui pénibles, voire dangereuses, des alertes qu’il a lui-même encouragées. À partir de 2029, une voiture trop bavarde pourra perdre des points dans sa note finale.
Une prise de conscience tardive
« Notre mission est de bannir les bips et les bongs », résume Matthew Avery. Pour lui, un conducteur qui désactive ses aides fait à peu près la même chose que s’il coupait son airbag ou détachait sa ceinture. Une surveillance du conducteur trop sensible ou une aide au maintien dans la voie trop autoritaire coûteront donc des points, et il prévient les constructeurs qu’Euro NCAP « arrive ».
Pour mesurer tout ça, l’organisme fait rouler depuis cette année chaque voiture testée sur 2 000 kilomètres de routes ouvertes, et relève au passage les fausses alertes. Il lui faut néanmoins des dizaines de milliers de kilomètres de données avant de note…

No one yet knows whether the stoppage is a pause or a lasting change.
Nvidia and its partners are still working out how to comply with Washington's new export controls, sources have told the Financial Times, and that process will decide how long the freeze lasts. Nvidia declined to comment. Dell, Supermicro, ByteDance and Aolani did not respond to requests for comment.
The four countries matter because Chinese AI developers have favored them as places to reach Nvidia hardware that Washington restricts from export. They matter to Nvidia, too: the company booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72% in 12 months, according to its accounts. That unit also carries some of Nvidia's Taiwan and China revenue.
Many Chinese companies have skirted the export rules by renting the chips instead of buying them. Cloud providers buy servers loaded with Nvidia processors and lease the computing time to customers, including Chinese ones. The US Commerce Department introduced new rules last week meant to end that practice.

El diseño es de Neel Adwani, doctorando en ingeniería eléctrica y computación, junto con Muhaiminul Islam Akash, Saffia Ouali y Ethan Liu, bajo la dirección del profesor Cong Wang. Adwani dijo que la cifra de menos de USD 650 incluye los servomotores (pequeños motores que mueven cada articulación), la placa de control, el filamento de impresión y las varillas de acero. El estudio, publicado en el repositorio arXiv, sostiene que el diseño reduce la barrera de entrada para quienes desarrollan manos robóticas.
Cómo es el diseño de la mano robótica
La mayoría de las manos robóticas económicas mueven los dedos con cables, similares a tendones. Según Adwani, esos cables se estiran, se resbalan y necesitan ajustes constantes. PHD-Hand los reemplaza por varillas y articulaciones rígidas, un sistema que evita ese mantenimiento.

Durch KI ist Content nun Massenware. Binnen weniger Minuten ist ein Text erstellt. Die Hürde, vor einem leeren Blatt zu sitzen und den ersten Gedanken zu formulieren, fällt weg. Allerdings hat der KI-Einsatz einen erheblichen Nachteil: Die Ergebnisse sind Texte mit einer frappierenden Gleichförmigkeit und auffällig gut strukturierten Textbausteinen. Sie arbeitet mit Statistik, ihr fehlen Edge-Cases und Outlier, weshalb sich jeder Inhalt irgendwann liest, wie der des Nachbarn.

The Senate committee has requested several changes to the federal government’s Lawful Access (Bill C-22) bill.
The national security, defence, and veterans affairs committee spent parts of Tuesday and Wednesday reviewing Bill C-22 clause by clause and agreed to further amend it.

For context, Bill C-22 is designed to make it easier for both police and intelligence agencies to intercept private or encrypted data as part of an investigation (which a UN human rights watchdog said violates human rights). The bill would allow the government to compel tech companies to change their systems to preserve data and then turn it over to intelligence or law enforcement.
Part of the changes include amending the bill to further clarify the definition of “systemic vulnerability” to cover the risk that secure information could be accessed. Another change made Wednesday would allow telecom providers to ask the Public Safety Minister to consult a new technical advisory committee on whether a directive would introduce a new vulnerability. The minister would also be able to consult this advisory committee proactively.

After 20 years of existence, X, the social network formerly known as Twitter, has finally added parental controls for teenagers, giving parents and guardians a way to manage what their kids see and interact with on the platform. But unlike most platforms’ implementation of such controls, X is putting its own spin on the system by giving teens a say in the matter.
The company said accounts belonging to 13-to-17-year-olds will be set to “protected mode” by default, meaning they won’t be able to see sensitive content, and won’t be served targeted ads. However, X is allowing teenagers to retain a measure of control over their accounts, letting them see what restrictions were made to their accounts. Parents and guardians will also not be able to read their teens’ private messages, see search or viewing history, or post as their teen.
The controls let parents see how much time their teen spends on X per week, set daily limits, require their approval for new followers, limit feed recommendations and videos to already followed accounts, filter specific words, turn off sensitive media, specify who can send their teen DMs, and see who they are messaging.
The controls arrive months after X came under fire for a lack of controls preventing the platform’s AI chatbot from being used to generate sexualized images of children and women. The social network has also long been rife with child sexual abuse material, misinformation, AI bots, and openly lets users post porn.

articles.title: Los los cocineros y nutricionistas coinciden: "El salmón será más saludable y jugoso si lo cocinas con zumo de naranja en vez de con aceite."
articles.summary:
Si tienes un par de lomos de salmón en la nevera y te apetece algo diferente de la plancha de siempre, puedes probar de una receta de salmón a la naranja y tirar de esta fruta para preparar una salsa en la que el pescado termina de cocinarse. Además, tanto los cocineros como los nutricionistas coinciden en que con este zumo el resultado será más jugoso y saludable que con aceite.
Características del salmón. El salmón un pescado graso con las propiedades típicas de los pescados azules: 12 gramos de lípidos por cada 100 gramos de porción comestible, una cantidad parecida a la de los atunes o los reos, y aportes importantes de ácidos grasos monoinsaturados y poliinsaturados, entre ellos omega 3 y omega 6. Además, también es una rica fuente de proteínas.
Lo que vas a necesitar. Para la receta hacen falta dos lomos de salmón, 200 mililitros de zumo de naranja y un par de rodajas de la misma fruta, a los que se suman una cucharada de salsa de soja, otra de miel, una cucharadita de jengibre rallado, un diente de ajo, una cucharada de aceite, sal y pimienta. Al final también se utiliza cebollino para decorar, aunque no aparece en la lista de ingredientes.
Primero, la salsa. Por último, se pica el diente de ajo y se añade a la mezcla.

articles.title: La inseguridad se ha convertido en una condición estructural de Internet
articles.summary:
Llevo años escuchando la cantinela de que la ciberseguridad es, sobre todo, un problema técnico. Lo primero que nos dicen los expertos es instalar actualizaciones, usar contraseñas complejas y distintas, activar la verificación en dos pasos, y, en el caso de negocios, contratar a alguien que sepa lo que hace con tus sistemas. Siguen siendo consejos razonables y muy recomendables. Lo que pasa es que parece que ya no son suficientes.
Estoy convencido de que la seguridad digital ya no es una estado al que se llega, sino una carrera sin línea de meta. Y con la inteligencia artificial, la velocidad de esa carrera ha subido a lo bestia.
Ojo, la IA no ha inventado el hackeo. Los fallos de software, las credenciales robadas, los errores humanos y las cadenas de suministro inseguras existían mucho antes, y no van a desaparecer porque el eslabón más débil seguimos siendo las personas. Lo que ha cambiado es la economía del ataque. Herramientas de IA pueden automatizar la búsqueda de vulnerabilidades, encadenar técnicas conocidas y escanear sistemas expuestos a Internet con una rapidez y un coste antes impensables. El problema no es tanto que la IA descubra ataques nuevos, que también, sino que hace más barato, rápido y accesible explotar los fallos que ya estaban ahí.

The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center company Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy. She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week.
What’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects new intelligence or political pressure is the big question.

articles.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
articles.summary:
Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.
A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.
Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don’t digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that …

Hala Mobility combines EV rentals, delivery jobs, and financial services for gig workers
Hyderabad-based startup Hala Mobility provides electric vehicles to delivery riders, connects them with delivery companies, and offers early-salary financing and accident insurance.
Delivery riders can cover 100 to 120 km a day, often on petrol vehicles that aren’t designed for such intensive use. Rising fuel prices add to their operating costs.
Electric vehicles (EVs) can reduce these expenses, and delivery companies are encouraging riders to make the switch. However, riders who cannot afford or access an EV have little choice but to continue using petrol vehicles.
Access to a vehicle is only part of the problem. Riders also need to know how far it can travel on a charge, where to charge it, and where to get it serviced. For companies managing large EV fleets, the challenges extend to monitoring battery health, battery swaps, energy consumption, and maintenance schedules.
Hyderabad-based Hala Mobility aims to address these gaps through an EV fleet-as-a-service and multi-modal shared mobility platform that allows riders and delivery companies to use EVs without purchasing them.
Through the Hala app, riders can rent, lease or finance vehicles. Hala was founded in 2019 by Srikanth Reddy Kalakonda, Founder and CEO, and Co-founder Snehith Reddy Meda.
